title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from this page and its neighbours. k is an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0. X is a curve of type (g,ν) over k, with a point x. The relevant groups are:
- π_{X,x} = π_1^et(X,x).
- M_{g,ν} = π_1 of the universal curve over the moduli stack M_{g,ν} over Q.
- N_{g,ν} = π_1 of the moduli stack over Q. It is an extension of Gal(Q̄/Q) by the profinite Teichmüller group T̂_{g,ν}.

P_{X,x} is a torsor under M_{g,ν} and Q_X is a torsor under N_{g,ν}. They are the torsors of identifications of the 'arithmetic fundamental group package' of (X,x) with the standard one, the standard one being built from a reference complex curve (X_0,x_0).

Previous page. Pushing Q_X out along N_{g,ν} → Gal(Q̄/Q) gives a Gal-torsor R_X. This torsor is canonically Isom(Q̄, Q̃), where Q̃ is the algebraic closure of Q in k. Hence a reduction of the structure group of Q_X from N_{g,ν} to T̂^+_{g,ν} (equivalently of P_{X,x} from M_{g,ν} to Ĝ^+_{g,ν}) is the same as an isomorphism Q̄ ≅ Q̃, i.e. an embedding of Q̄ into k.

This page.
1. Fix an embedding φ: k → C. Then X^φ = X ⊗_φ C is a Riemann surface of type (g,ν).
2. Its topological π_1 is a discrete group. By Riemann existence its profinite completion is π_{X,x}, so φ gives a discrete dense subgroup π_1^top ⊂ π_{X,x}. Grothendieck calls this a 'discrétification arithmétique' of the profinite group.
3. The same works for the whole moduli/universal-curve package. The comparison is with the orientation determined by the complex structure, hence the '+'.
4. So φ reduces the structure group of P_{X,x} from M_{g,ν} to the discrete group G^+_{g,ν} (π_1 of the universal curve over Teichmüller theory, i.e. the extension of the mapping class group by π_1 of the surface). Equivalently, it reduces Q_X from N_{g,ν} to the discrete mapping class group T^+_{g,ν}. This gives the sub-torsors P^φ_{X,x} ⊂ P_{X,x} and Q^φ_X ⊂ Q_X of (21).
5. Taking closures (profinite completions) gives (22): reductions to Ĝ^+ and T̂^+.
6. By the previous page, the data (22) is just an isomorphism Q̄ → Q̃. So the completed data only remembers φ restricted to Q̃, the algebraic part of the embedding.

Final remark, left open: Grothendieck 'thinks' that the discrete data P^φ_{X,x} (or Q^φ_X), taken for all X and all (g,ν), determines φ itself, transcendental part included.

Purpose: to separate what the arithmetic fundamental group sees. The profinite structure sees only the Galois or algebraic part of an embedding into C. The discrete Teichmüller structure, as a sub-torsor of the profinite torsor, might encode the whole complex embedding.
errors: No real mathematical error. The passage from (21) to (22) needs the closure of the discrete T^+ in N_{g,ν} to be its full profinite completion T̂^+. That holds because π_1 of the moduli stack over Q̄ is the profinite completion of the mapping class group, but it is used without comment.

The conjecture at the end is stated without argument. One subtlety: under complex conjugation φ ↦ φ̄, the discrete subgroup π_1^top of each curve is presumably the same subset of π̂, but the orientation flips. So recovering φ must use the oriented (+) data, or else only the pair {φ, φ̄} can be expected.
The notation for Q̄ versus Q̃ (algebraic closure in C versus in k) is used loosely between this page and the previous one.

ideas.what: An embedding k → C gives a reduction of the profinite torsor Q_X (structure group π_1(M_{g,ν,Q})) to the discrete oriented mapping class group T^+_{g,ν}. This 'arithmetic discretification' of π̂_1 comes from comparison with topological π_1.
ideas.modern_name: Betti/topological structure on étale fundamental groups via Riemann existence; comparison torsor between Betti and étale π_1
ideas.usually_credited_to: Riemann existence/comparison: SGA1 (Grothendieck), Artin. The torsor viewpoint for moduli of curves is implicit in Ihara, Nakamura and others' work on Gal(Q̄/Q) acting on π̂_1(M_{g,n}).
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the Teichmüller tower with discrete and profinite versions, but not in this torsor-reduction form as far as I know.

ideas.what: The profinite completion of that discrete reduction is equivalent to an isomorphism Q̄ ≅ Q̃. So it recovers only φ restricted to the algebraic closure of Q in k.
ideas.modern_name: Galois torsor of fibre functors and the outer Galois action on π̂_1(M_{g,n})

ideas.what: Conjecture: the discrete sub-torsors P^φ_{X,x} ⊂ P_{X,x}, over all curves X/k and all (g,ν), determine the embedding φ: k → C, including its transcendental part.
ideas.modern_name: Faithfulness of the Aut(C)-action on Betti lattices inside étale (profinite) fundamental groups; non-abelian analogue of Betti–étale comparison in Deligne's absolute Hodge cycles
ideas.usually_credited_to: No explicit attribution known. Related themes: Serre's conjugate varieties with non-isomorphic π_1; Deligne's absolute Hodge cycles (1982).

missed.claim: Grothendieck conjectures that the family of discrete 'arithmetic discretifications' P^φ_{X,x} (equivalently Q^φ_X), for all curves X over k, determines φ: k → C. The profinite data determines only φ|Q̃. This makes the discrete lattice π_1^top ⊂ π̂_1 an invariant that encodes transcendental information about the embedding, a non-abelian 'period' structure.
missed.quote: Mais je pense que la connaissance de P^φ_{X,x} (ou Q^φ_X) lui-même, pour tout X (et tout g,ν) définit φ ....
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a precise anabelian-style question I do not recall seeing stated in the literature. Does the action of wild automorphisms of C on Betti lattices inside étale π_1 of curves (or of M_{g,n}) separate embeddings? It is the non-abelian counterpart of Betti–étale comparison in Deligne's absolute Hodge cycles, and of Serre-type phenomena for conjugate varieties. It could be tested even on elliptic curves, via lattices H_1(E^φ, Z) inside T̂(E).

missed.claim: The page frames the discrete Teichmüller/mapping class group structure as a reduction of structure group of a profinite Galois-arithmetic torsor, parametrised by complex embeddings. This links the Teichmüller tower to the torsor of comparison isomorphisms (a 'period torsor' for π_1), anticipating motivic-Galois/period-torsor viewpoints on π_1, but in profinite-discrete rather than de Rham–Betti form.
missed.quote: structure de "discrétification arithmétique" des groupes profinis π_{X,x}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests studying the torsor of Betti structures on étale π_1(M_{g,n}) as an Aut(C)-object. That bridges Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory with the period-torsor/absolute-Hodge viewpoint, a link not systematically developed.

deep.surprise_reason: Most of the page is a routine torsor reformulation of Riemann existence and the Galois action. The closing conjecture is the notable part: discrete Teichmüller structures over all curves should recover the full, transcendental complex embedding. It is a natural, crisp question that seems unaddressed in print, though possibly folklore.
transcription_corrections: 'K' in the first displayed line should be lowercase 'k' (the base field), matching the neighbouring pages.
'Un [?] plongement' reads more like 'Un tel plongement' (or 'Ce plongement').
In (21) the equivalence sign is written in parentheses '(⇔)' in the first line.
The isomorphism near the bottom reads 'Q̃ → Q̄' (one with tilde, one with bar), not 'Q̄ → Q̄'.
The struck word before 'Ces données' is 'dont', replaced by 'donc'.
